fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -race ./internal/run -run TestScaledClock shows: at scale 1000 Sleep(30*time.Second) returns within 100 ms of real time and Now has advanced at least 30 s; real time spent outside Sleep (a 50 ms time.Sleep between two Now calls) advances Now by about 50 ms, not 50 s; Sleep(time.Microsecond) still waits at least 1 ms; Sleep and Now called from several goroutines pass under -race; with RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE unset or empty the chosen clock is RealClock; failure cases: values 0, -5, 1.5 and abc each give RealClock and no panic. Touches internal/run/engine.go or a new internal/run/clock.go and its _test.go. Must not change RealClock, the Engine's nil-Clock default or any workflow's poll or backoff value.
fields.statement: internal/run has a scaled Clock, chosen by RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE=<n>, whose Sleep(d) waits d/n of real time (never less than 1 ms) and whose Now is the wall clock plus the time its Sleeps skipped, safe for concurrent use; with the variable unset, empty or not a positive integer the engine keeps RealClock.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -v ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-ship-conflict-fix|run-ship-ci-fix|run-ship-main-dispatch-fail|arbiter-agent-tabs|plan-workflow-ci-infra-wait)$' passes with each script's elapsed under 30 s (2026-11-15: 195, 173, 130, 108 and 96 s); go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestRunClock' shows runClock is RealClock with the variable unset and the scaled clock with it set; failure case: a script that clears it (env RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE=) runs on RealClock, shown by a short wait-timeout script in cmd/rhiza/testdata/script. Speedup measure (orchestrator, quiet VM): go clean -testcache && /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza, against 639 s. Touches internal/api/run.go, run_spawn.go, api.go, ship.go, session.go, ship_deploy.go, their tests, and cmd/rhiza/main_test.go. Must not change a production interval, a workflow .toml, or the daemon, feed and session-limit tickers.
fields.statement: When RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE is set, every wait a run makes goes by the scaled clock: internal/api's runClock (run.start and run.resume polls, wait conditions and backoff, session_run.go and session_message.go waits), the spawn poll in run_spawn.go, the default ctx.Sleep in api.go, ship.go and session.go, and ship_deploy.go's interval and its deadline; cmd/rhiza/main_test.go's Setup sets it to 1000 for every script, so the builtin workflows' 30 s polls and 2 min backoff cost milliseconds in scripts.

fields.reasoning: Clock.Now is used only for elapsed time within one process (internal/run engine.go wait, internal/api session_message.go typePointer), so a per-process offset is enough. A Now multiplied by the scale would count real work, such as a 50 ms process start, as 50 s and fire step and message timeouts early, changing poll counts and outcomes; adding only skipped sleep time keeps each loop's poll count as in production. A loop that sleeps scaled but measures its deadline with time.Now, as ship_deploy.go does, would poll 1000 times as often. runClock is a package variable read by concurrent goroutines, so the offset needs a lock or atomic.
fields.statement: The scaled clock's Now is the wall clock plus the time its Sleeps skipped (each Sleep(d) adds d minus the real time it waited), not the wall clock multiplied by the scale, and it is safe for concurrent use; every loop that sleeps on it measures its deadline with the same clock's Now
